text: A coding agent's run whose provider is briefly unavailable tries again (#261). At capacity, rate-limited, overloaded, high demand or a dropped connection counts, in Codex's and Claude Code's own words, and for Claude Code first from its own fields: the error's typed cause, the API's status and its kind. An account limit and an MCP server that didn't start don't count, and Codex's reconnect notices don't decide how a run ended. Every draft, plan, build and review retries in the same workspace with the same job and agent after one, two and four minutes, four attempts in all, as one run. Refining D-0154, the run's one deadline starts at the first attempt's turn and covers the waits and later turns, and each wait gives Codex's turn locks back. The run keeps one tool-call allowance, named in each MCP server's configuration, and only what's left of Claude Code's budget and turns or Codex's steps; usage sums the attempts. A run whose provider stays unavailable, or whose deadline ends a later attempt, fails as provider unavailable with the last error: a draft proposes nothing and says drafting again is all it needs, and a build publishes nothing and stops partway, so a writer's retry builds it again, review included. Built by hand while the factory waits for Codex budget.
